subject: MSA redlines — injunctive relief and arbitration fallback
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@novaplace.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Li <susan@novaplace.com>, Novaplace Legal <legal@novaplace.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Novaplace MSA redline — injunctive relief and forum clause

Evelyn — attaching our redline to the MSA (see attachment). Two points we wanted to flag before your legal team dives in: 1) we struck Redwood's injunctive-relief carve to limit expedited relief to "urgent IP or confidentiality harms" only; 2) we propose a mandatory arbitration clause for commercial disputes, but carve out injunctive relief to courts in New York (local counsel recommends).

Can you confirm Redwood's position on: (a) preserving a broad injunctive carve versus a narrow IP/confidentiality-only carve, and (b) whether Redwood will accept New York courts as the injunctive-relief forum if arbitration otherwise applies?

We'd like to get to a final MSA by the end of next week if possible.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Senior Counsel, Novaplace
Attachment: Novaplace_MSA_redline_20270510.docx

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@novaplace.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Novaplace MSA redline — injunctive relief and forum clause

Thanks Daniel — received and reviewing. Looping in our legal and commercial leads for a quick internal alignment so we can respond with a single proposal. Preliminary thoughts: Redwood's standard is to preserve the ability to seek emergency equitable relief in courts for customer-data/availability incidents as well as IP/confidentiality; we prefer a broader carve that includes preservation of access (not just IP). If Novaplace needs arbitration for broader disputes we can consider a hybrid (arbitration for most claims; courts for interim injunctive relief).

Jonas / Marissa / Rishi — can you weigh in on whether we're comfortable limiting the court carve to New York (as Novaplace proposes) or whether we should push for Redwood's home state (California) or a neutral seat? Please advise on commercial impact.

Evelyn
VP, Legal & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Novaplace MSA redline — injunctive relief and forum clause

Evelyn — quick note from legal ops. From an operational/risk standpoint we should: 1) keep the injunctive carve fairly broad (availability, data preservation, IP, confidentiality), 2) accept an "injunctive relief in court" carve but limit venue to either CA or NY (NY acceptable for larger east-coast customers, but CA is our preference), and 3) if we concede NY, add language that any emergency order must be narrowly tailored and that arbitration remains the exclusive remedy otherwise.

If commercial wants the deal to move faster, accept NY but we will seek specific narrowing language on scope and expedited notice/fall-back to arbitration for final relief. I can draft suggested language.

— Jonas
Associate GC (Contracts)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:47:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Novaplace MSA redline — injunctive relief and forum clause

Evelyn / team — commercial view: Novaplace is strategic (pilot + potential Dedicated upsell). We should prioritize time-to-sign but not at the cost of an open-ended court exposure. Proposed commercial compromise: accept Novaplace's NY carve but add (i) a 7-day escalation/notice period to allow mediation/arbitration to begin, and (ii) a "limited relief" clause that injunctive measures must be limited to preservation of evidence, immediate data-segmentation, or temporary access controls. If legal agrees to that narrow scope, we give them a quick yes.

Marissa
Head of Sales, East Coast Accounts

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@novaplace.com>
Cc: Novaplace Legal <legal@novaplace.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 16:42:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Novaplace MSA redline — injunctive relief and forum clause

Daniel — thanks for the patience. We've reviewed Novaplace's redline and discussed commercially. Redwood's proposed path: 

- Redwood will agree to an arbitration-first regime for substantive disputes.
- We can accept your request that courts in New York handle interim injunctive relief, on the condition that: (a) the injunctive carve is expressly limited to preservation of evidence, protection of IP, prevention of ongoing unauthorized access to customer data, and interim measures necessary to preserve system availability; (b) §X.Y includes a 7-calendar-day notice-and-escalation window for the parties to attempt expedited arbitration/mediated relief before filing in court, except where irreparable harm would be imminent; and (c) any emergency order must be narrowly tailored and limited in scope and duration.

We have attached a short diff with the proposed injunctive-paragraph edits for your review. If Novaplace can accept that language we can issue a redline to the rest of the MSA and aim to sign this week.

Proposed next steps: Novaplace confirms acceptance or provides one round of edits by EOD Wednesday; we finalize and circulate an execution copy.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
VP, Legal & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Proposed-Injunction-Paragraph.diff.txt
